applies_to: GE Multilin EPM 6000 power meters on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the GE EPM 6000: 262 Analog Inputs, 37 polled by default. Polled values are total watts, VARs and VA, phase voltages and currents, PF, frequency, neutral current, energy and the averages; the long tail of per-phase, THD and min/max values is unpolled.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile GE_EPM6000_PowerMeter_a_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the maker's Modbus register document (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/GEK-106558D.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 37 of the 262 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (Watts 3-Ph total; VARs 3-Ph total; VAs 3-Ph total...); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

integration.summary: Map total watts (3-phase), delivered energy (Wh) and received energy (Wh) first. The listed objects are read-only.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
